info.description: Linear equations, matrices, determinants. Real and abstract vector spaces, subspaces and linear transformations; basis and change of basis. Complex numbers. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors; diagonalization. Inner products and orthogonality; least squares problems. Applications. Subject is presented with an abstract emphasis and includes proofs of the basic theorems.
info.title: Algebra I: Linear Algebra
info.departmentalUgradNotes: Final Examinations: Students are expected to remain available for the entire final examination period published in the Academic Calendar. info.gradingNotes:
In addition to the above, students will write concept quizzes, Pass/Fail basis, each with 2 retakes [3 quizzes].

Policy on generative AI

The prevalence of powerful new AI-based tools (chatbots and agents) is changing many facets of life. Here’s one sobering opinion: students are uniquely vulnerable to becoming redundant if they don’t train their mathematical brain. Relying on AI chatbots measurably decreases our cognitive abilities. You are here to learn the material; AI will empower you once you have done so.

With this in mind: I expect you to treat the training of your mind as an existentially important activity. Homeworks won’t be graded, and if you get solutions from the web or from AI – there is ample evidence that you will perform poorly on the examinations. The use of AI tools is strictly prohibited on the graded portions of this class.

The following is the default policy in the Department of Mathematics. Please check your course syllabus whether the instructor has chosen a different policy for your class, otherwise the following policy applies.
 
To receive a grade of C- or higher the student must receive a passing grade on the weighted average of exams in the course. What constitutes a passing grade is up to the discretion of the instructor, though the default is a grade of 50% or higher.
info.courseDetails:
Linear Equations

  • Systems of Linear Equations, Row Reduction and Echelon Form
  • Vectors, Vector Equations, Matrices
  • The Matrix Equation Ax=b
  • Solution Sets of Linear Systems
  • Matrix Inverse
  • Linear Independence, Rank and Dimension
  • Introduction to Linear Transformations
  • The Matrix of a Linear Transformation
Vector Spaces
  • Vector Spaces and Subspaces
  • Null Spaces, Column Spaces, and Linear Transformations
  • Linearly Independent Sets; Bases for Subspaces
  • Coordinate Systems
  • The Dimension of a Vector Space
  • Change of Basis
Complex Numbers
  • The Complex Plane, Complex Conjugate, and Magnitude
  • Polar Form, De Moivre's Formula and Euler's Formula
  • Roots of Quadratic Polynomials
Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
  • Complex Eigenvalues
  • Computing Eigenpairs
  • Diagonalization
  • Eigenvectors and Linear Transformations
  • Application: The Leslie Age Distribution model
Orthogonality and Least Squares
  • Inner Product, Length and Orthogonality
  • Orthogonal Sets
  • Orthogonal Projections
  • The Gram-Schmidt Process
  • Application: Least Squares Problems
Matrix Decompositions
  • LU, QR, SVD
Determinants
  • Determinants and their Properties
